title: Determination of nitrogen balance in agroecosystems
author: Sainju

steps.title: Measure soil N and bulk density
steps.instruction: Determine soil total N concentration in each sample using the Bremner method and determine bulk density of each soil layer with the core method; then calculate soil total N content for each layer with STN = STNc × BD × T × 10,000 (STN in kg N ha⁻¹, STNc in g N kg⁻¹, BD in Mg m⁻³, T in m, conversion factor = 10,000). Perform the calculation for samples taken at the beginning and end of the experiment, adjust bulk density and STN using the equivalent soil mass method, and sum the STN values of all layers to obtain whole‑profile N content.

substeps.instruction: Collect soil samples from each layer.
Analyze total N concentration (g N kg⁻¹) following Bremner [3].
Measure bulk density (Mg m⁻³) with the core method [6].
Apply the formula STN = STNc × BD × T × 10,000.
Adjust values with the equivalent soil mass method [5].
Add layer‑wise STN to get profile N (kg N ha⁻¹).

steps.title: Calculate N fertilization rate
steps.instruction: Determine the N fertilization rate by first measuring soil NO₃‑N, NH₄‑N, total N and bulk density to 60 cm depth, then compute their contents (kg N ha⁻¹) as concentration × BD × layer thickness; finally apply Na = Nr – (NO₃‑N + 0.01 × [STN – NH₄‑N – NO₃‑N]) where Na is the fertilization rate (kg N ha⁻¹) and Nr is the recommended rate. Use 1 % mineralization of soil organic N (or 2 % for high‑organic‑matter irrigated soils). If organic N data are unavailable or NH₄‑N is negligible, use only soil NO₃‑N in the equation. For rates not adjusted to soil N, use the recommended rate directly. Expected accuracy is ±5–10 % of applied N; reduce uncertainty by intensive, composite soil sampling.

substeps.instruction: Collect soil to 60 cm from several locations within each treatment, composite, air‑dry, and grind to 2 mm.
Determine NO₃‑N and NH₄‑N concentrations (Mulvaney [9]).
Determine total N concentration and bulk density as in step 1.
Calculate NO₃‑N, NH₄‑N, and total N contents (kg N ha⁻¹) = concentration × BD × thickness.
Insert values into Eq. 6 to obtain Na.
Apply the appropriate mineralization factor (1 % or 2 %).
If organic N unavailable or NH₄‑N negligible, set the term 0.01 × [STN – NH₄‑N – NO₃‑N] to 0.01 × [STN – NO₃‑N].
Report Na with ±5–10 % accuracy.

steps.title: Assess symbiotic N fixation (legumes)
steps.instruction: Measure fresh grain and above‑ground biomass yields of legumes, dry subsamples at 65 °C to constant weight, determine dry matter yield, analyze total N concentration (g N kg⁻¹) in each plant part using the Bremner method, calculate N content (kg N ha⁻¹) as dry yield × N concentration, and compute biological N fixation with the appropriate equation: if only grain N is removed, use Biological N fixation = 0.7 × (Biomass N + 0.33 × total aboveground biomass N); if total aboveground biomass N (including forage) is removed, use Biological N fixation = 0.7 × 0.33 × total aboveground biomass N.

substeps.instruction: Harvest fresh grain and stems/leaves; record fresh weights.
Dry representative subsamples at 65 °C until constant weight (typically 3–7 days).
Weigh dried subsamples to obtain dry matter yield.
Grind a portion of each dried component to <1 mm.
Determine total N concentration (g N kg⁻¹) by the Bremner method [3].
Calculate N content = dry matter (kg ha⁻¹) × N concentration (g kg⁻¹) / 1000.
Apply Eq. 7 or Eq. 8 depending on whether only grain N or total aboveground biomass N is removed.

steps.title: Calculate fixation for cover/green manure crops
steps.instruction: When total aboveground biomass N is returned to the soil (cover or green‑manure legumes), compute biological N fixation as Biological N fixation = 0.7 × 1.33 × total aboveground biomass N (kg N ha⁻¹).

steps.title: Determine crop N removal at harvest
steps.instruction: Harvest the target crop (by hand or machine) from a known area, weigh grain and/or biomass to obtain fresh yield, dry a representative sample at 65 °C for 3–7 days to get dry matter yield, grind a subsample to <1 mm, determine N concentration using the Bremner method, and calculate crop N removal as crop yield (kg ha⁻¹) × N concentration (g kg⁻¹) / 1000. Report uncertainty as ±15–25 % of total N uptake; reduce it by increasing the harvested area and using accurate N analysis.

substeps.instruction: Harvest and weigh crop from a measured plot area.
Dry a subsample at 65 °C for 3–7 days; weigh to obtain dry matter.
Grind dried material to <1 mm.
Analyze N concentration (g N kg⁻¹) with the Bremner method.
Calculate N removal = dry yield (kg ha⁻¹) × N concentration / 1000.
State uncertainty (±15–25 %).

steps.title: Estimate or measure denitrification loss
steps.instruction: If possible, measure N loss through denitrification using published methods (e.g., 15N isotope method). When measurement is impractical, estimate loss based on soil organic matter and drainage conditions. For total N loss from inorganic fertilizer and manure, subtract ammonia volatilization loss from the N fertilization rate, then add N inputs from fertilizer, wet and dry deposition, and irrigation. Note that ammonia volatilization loss differs between inorganic fertilizer and manure, and denitrification loss from manure is twice that from fertilizer; calculate each component separately if both are applied, then sum to obtain total denitrification loss. Report uncertainty as ±20–50 % of applied N and describe ways to reduce it.

substeps.instruction: Choose a measurement method (e.g., 15N isotope) if feasible.
If not, estimate denitrification loss using literature values for organic‑matter content and drainage.
Determine ammonia volatilization loss for each N source (inorganic fertilizer, manure).
Subtract volatilization loss from the N fertilization rate.
Add N inputs from fertilizer, wet deposition, dry deposition, and irrigation to obtain total N input.
Apply the factor that manure denitrification loss = 2 × fertilizer denitrification loss; calculate each separately if both are used.
Sum the component losses to get total denitrification loss.
Report uncertainty (±20–50 %).
